chapters.title: BOM Impact on Cost Control and Manufacturing

features.name: Bill of Materials definition
features.description: The BOM is the list that defines the components required to produce an item. It acts as a recipe and drives material planning, consumption, and costing.

features.name: Production order replenishment
features.description: Items can be replenished through production order when you need multi-step operations, machine centers, or capacity planning with associated BOMs.

features.name: Assembly replenishment
features.description: Assembly is used for straightforward processes and simple labor-only work, with an associated BOM defining the components.
caveats: Used only for simple labor-only processes

features.name: BOM formulas for units of measure
features.description: You can use formulas for standardized units of measure in BOM component quantities, allowing flexible quantity calculations.

features.name: Where-used analysis
features.description: For each item listed on the bill of materials, you can see where it is used using the where-used action.

features.name: BOM item versions with ending dates
features.description: You can set ending dates for item versions in a BOM, allowing transition from pre-produced items to production BOMs on a specific date without major alterations.
caveats: Used for managing transitions between item and BOM versions

features.name: Phantom BOMs
features.description: Phantom BOMs allow you to replace pre-produced items with production BOMs from a specific date onward without major alterations to the main product.

features.name: Production BOM version management
features.description: You can define multiple versions of a production BOM with different starting dates, so production automatically picks the correct BOM based on the production date.

features.name: Production BOM version comparison
features.description: You can compare different versions of a single production BOM to see how the components vary across versions.

features.name: Production order creation from BOM
features.description: Production orders automatically populate component lines and routings by refreshing the order, pulling from the appropriate BOM version based on the due date.
caveats: Version selection is automatic based on due date but can be manually overridden

features.name: Production order components action
features.description: The components action in a production order allows exploration of which items are required for production of each product line.

quotes.text: The bill of materials, also called BOM, is the list that defines the components required to produce an item.
quotes.why_it_matters: Core definition of the BOM concept central to the entire manufacturing process.

quotes.text: Choose production order when you need multi-step operations, machine centers, or capacity planning.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies when to use production order versus assembly for replenishment, a key design decision.

quotes.text: BOM acts as the recipe and drives material planning, consumption, and costing.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the fundamental role of BOMs in manufacturing operations and their impact on business outcomes.

quotes.text: The item version of reservoir assembly has an ending date of 1st of June, when the production BOM version starts being used.
quotes.why_it_matters: Demonstrates how BOM versions enable controlled transitions between different manufacturing approaches without disruption.

quotes.text: For more complex modifications, you can define new versions and their starting date, so that production will pick the correct production BOM.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows the flexibility of BOM versioning for managing product changes and evolution over time.

quotes.text: Once those fields are defined, we can refresh the production order to automatically populate the order lines with components and routings.
quotes.why_it_matters: Demonstrates automation in production order creation that pulls BOM components and routings based on due date.

quotes.text: An accurate bill of material definition improves cost visibility and gives you better control over costs and product changes as your business evolves.
quotes.why_it_matters: Summarizes the strategic value of accurate BOMs for cost control and organizational agility.
